target_customer: Originally Indian startups and SMEs buying payroll, HR and IT; now creators who pay for AI video
problem: Indian founders needed one place for payroll, HR and compliance. The company later restarted as an AI video maker for creatives.
business_model: SaaS subscription (original HR product); freemium subscription with Pro, Ultra and Max plans (current video product)
product_category: HR and payroll platform, then AI video creation

founders.name: Deepit Patil
education: IIT Delhi, computational mechanics, dropped out

competitors.name: RazorpayX Payroll
competitors.what: automated payroll and compliance software for Indian startups
competitors.funding_then: part of Razorpay, funding not stated

technical_complexity.rationale: Payroll and compliance software for India is rules heavy but standard engineering. The later AI video product orchestrates third party models.

defensibility.rationale: Many payroll vendors existed and no source shows a moat. Switching costs in payroll are modest for tiny teams.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbent payroll tools served the same startups; the original product was shut down, though no source ties that to incumbents.

market_need_then: Indian startups needed compliant payroll and HR; vendor pages show an active market of products aimed at startups, but no evidence on Craze demand.

branding.domain_note: Old crazehq.com now redirects to craze.ai per a secondary profile.

identity.voice_and_tone: Founder announced the old product as dead and relaunched, wording quoted as Craze is dead, long live Craze

rebrands.to: Craze AI (agent layer, then AI video)
rebrands.why: Original product shut down; date conflicts between 2025 and 2026 in secondary sources.

branding.community_and_virality: The shutdown announcement was posted on April Fools day according to a secondary profile and some commenters thought it was a joke; single source.

brand_strength.rationale: Several other companies use the name Craze and press about the brand was not found.

pivots.from: HR, payroll and IT platform for India
pivots.why: Founders announced the old product shut down; reason not public. Date conflicts (2025 vs 2026).

outcome_analysis: Craze entered YC in Summer 2022 as an HR and payroll platform for India and was backed by YC, Nexus Venture Partners and Soma Capital according to a profile. The founders later shut the original product and relaunched twice, ending in an AI video maker. The cause of the shutdown is not public. Funding is undisclosed, so the outcome is a restart rather than a clean success or failure.
notes: A 500K pre seed is reported only by a single aggregator (signalbase), unverified, so it is not a round. Investors YC, Nexus Venture Partners and Soma Capital come from an aggregator profile. Shutdown date conflicts between 2025 and 2026. Competitor pages are undated vendor pages, so source_date is null; no dated 2022 coverage was found. Team and location differ across sources (Mumbai, 8 to 12 people). The failure factor pivot_failed is a weak fit because the pivot outcome is still open. Completeness pass: the 500K seed dated 2022-09-06 rests on a single database (Caplight; Signalbase also reports 500K). A 2.22M convertible note dated 2022-11-22 rests on a single database (CB Insights, which totals 3.22M over 5 rounds, so the other rounds are missing). Both are database figures with no press confirmation.
